original_acceptance: test control cannot leak into production authority
The named outcome has actual source/build-bound evidence; unsupported, pending, failed and unperformed checks remain explicit.
decision: Add one registered df-engine integration test that composes the current VirtualClocks, SuppliedDice and SemanticReplay with df_engine::command_entry::decide_registered_command and its exact DispatchRegistry consumer. Keep the test handler and builders private to this integration test and reuse crates/df-engine/tests/support/fixture_model.rs. The testkit records and elapsed controls are fixtures; only the existing Engine and Rules staging contracts decide whether a supplied candidate can be staged.

contract_cases.asserted: A source-exact registered handler stages a canonical next-revision candidate; caller clock domains advance independently; SuppliedDice returns the same borrowed ActualDraw record; Engine forwards the original draw slice to the registered handler; input and current checkpoint remain unchanged.

contract_cases.case: Identity, actor reference and command basis refusal
contract_cases.asserted: Unknown member, unknown actor entity, and a future command basis receive exact existing structural error classes before handler invocation; fixture dice remains at ordinal zero with its record unconsumed.
Changed admitted rules pins return CheckpointError::RulesMismatch; an unregistered source returns DispatchError::UnsupportedSource; neither invokes the handler.
Independent logical/presentation advances work; logical regression and presentation overflow return typed errors and preserve both clock fields.

Exact accepted decision and AI job records are borrowed; wrong job generation, operation, policy, basis/run or pins refuse as ReplayError::Stale. SemanticReplay exposes no provider callback or authority-producing call.

unresolved_authority_and_source_gaps: Engine structural validation does not authenticate a sender or authorize control of an existing member/actor. This test checks only the existing unknown-member and unknown-actor-reference typed refusals. Existing-member/actor authorization remains Session/rules-owned and is not claimed here.

The fixture catalog and registered handler demonstrate the existing source-selector and pin plumbing; they do not qualify source provenance, prove standard mechanics, or establish production source-use rights.

The staged candidate is fixture-built through the canonical checkpoint types; it is not a reviewed rules golden or a state-hash/reducer/restart proof. Full RuleFixture source checksum, catalog/handler qualification and property/generative interaction coverage remain outside this bounded Design outcome.
No provider callable, storage, PostgreSQL, browser, paid-provider or production authority fixture is introduced.
alternatives_considered: A standalone df-testkit unit test would prove fixture-local behavior only and would miss the named production-authority boundary; rejected in favor of the registered Engine consumer.
A new Engine authorization method or guessed existing-actor denial would invent a contract contrary to the current source boundary; rejected.
A public fixture API, production dependency, provider substitute, or provider-call spy would expand authority and scope; rejected.

This deviation is included for the coordinator and reviewer; no claim of fully guarded source provenance is made. The initial private-ledger scratch serialization also stopped on a Python NameError before any target file write; the corrected M-wrapped SH|NB write succeeded.
